key_insight: AutoEnergyDesign uses an LLM agent to optimize building energy systems, reaching a roughly €3.53 million net present cost with far fewer simulations than conventional search baselines.
engineering_relevance: The framework could reduce simulation demands when sizing integrated energy systems, including photovoltaics, storage, heat pumps and other technologies—not solar cells themselves.
method: Propose constrained design changes using simulation history and structured memory.
Evaluate designs with year-long simulations and a 25-year net present cost objective.
Keep improvements and automatically revert unsuccessful changes through git.
evidence_signal: On one measured-load building case, three LLM variants underwent ten 50-simulation runs each; their best cost was 1.20% below TPE and 0.23% below an evolution strategy tested with 300 evaluations per seed.
watch_item: Evidence is limited to one building case, and reliability varied by model; broader validation and total computational cost assessment remain important.
paper_title: AutoEnergyDesign: An LLM-Driven Agent for Automatic Energy System Design Optimization
